findings.finding: Independently downloaded and visually inspected publisher's complete first-cello part, 78 bars. Exact title Hymnus for twelve cellos, Op.57, EB6847. Andante cantabile in G; bass, tenor and treble clefs; long exposed upper-register phrases, chromatic slurred motion, triplets and very soft entries. Watermark obscures portions but register, pace and overall part profile remain legible.
Publisher identifies original twelve-cello edition. This review concerns that scoring, not the viola-and-tenor audio on IMSLP.

grade.basis: Whole first-cello part supports advanced cello technique (approximately level5/ABRSM8 rather than sustained concerto virtuosity): fluent tenor/treble-register cantabile and chromatic intonation at a restrained tempo. Add one level for exposed unaccompanied tuning, blended entrances and balance across twelve independent cellos. Result6, pre-diploma, above the lyrical Webern Langsamer Satz5 anchor but below the broad technical demands of the diploma7 anchors. Only first part directly inspected; lower-part comparison remains provisional, hence medium confidence.

findings.finding: Visually inspected ACC2092 score opening: title Suite for Eight Violas, dedication In memoriam Lionel Tertis; all eight viola staves. Poco maestoso quarter54; upper-register melodic lines, clef changes, chromatic inflections and independent pizzicato support.
Printed p.5 includes Scherzo and Drone, Allegro vivo quarter120. Rapid semiquavers in upper parts, chromatic and accented gestures, double stops and ensemble-wide changes of articulation.
Printed p.13 shows end of Scherzo and opening of Chorale Lento quarter60: contrasting short upper-register figures and pizzicato interruptions, then exposed sustained eight-part harmony.

Printed p.15 opens Tarantella, Allegro con fuoco dotted-quarter132, 6/8: brisk articulated eighth-note figures, upper-register first viola, repeated accompaniment and coordinated pizzicato/arco changes. All four movements represented across inspected previews.

grade.basis: Across previews of all four movements, first-viola facility is approximately pre-diploma6: quick chromatic semiquavers, upper positions/treble clef, secure articulation and fast tarantella phrasing. Add one for independent eight-part timing, coordinated accents, balance and exposed chorale intonation. Diploma7 is above Dvorak American6 yet below Mendelssohn Octet8 in sustained technical breadth. No full-score claim: continuation beyond the published preview pages remains unseen; confidence medium.

findings.finding: Publisher identifies Klaus Trumpf arrangement for four double basses, FH2227, with score and four parts. Exact version established; original two-bass-and-piano scoring is not substituted in this review.

Visually inspected publisher's first score page (bars1–14). Printed arrangement credit Klaus Trumpf and four numbered bass staves. First and second bass exchange exposed upper-register treble-clef cantabile lines; third/fourth provide arco and pizzicato accompaniment; ornaments, chromaticism, clef changes and wide register shifts visible.

grade.basis: Professional8, chiefly the principal solo bass demand rather than an automatic quartet uplift. Publisher preview verifies the arrangement retains the exposed treble-register solo roles of Bottesini's concert duet; calibrated knowledge of Passione amorosa as a whole places its sustained high-thumb-position cantabile and bravura exchanges above diploma7, without the extreme demands warranting9–10. The arrangement's later pages are unseen: no specific later bar, double-stop passage or range maximum is asserted. First bass tentatively hardest from inspected page; second is also a solo-level role. Grade is medium-confidence expert inference from this preview plus knowledge of the source work, not a full-score audit.

findings.finding: Independently downloaded complete32-page AVS009 edition. Read preface and visually inspected the entire first-viola part (PDFpp2–5), plus full-score PDFpp22 and24 for comparison of all four parts. Exact original four-viola setting, editor David M. Bynog. First part spans lyrical Sehr leicht und lebhaft, Sehr schnell section atbar66, springing-bow chromatic semiquavers and high treble-register runs, then expressive slower music and muted close; second/third/fourth also exchange independent fast entries. First has greatest sustained upper-register and passagework demand.

grade.basis: Advanced5 player demand: fluent high positions, fast chromatic semiquavers, varied slur/staccato bowing, intermittent double stops, soft spiccato and treble/alto reading. Add one for interlocking entries, matched light articulation and exposed chromatic tuning, giving pre-diploma6. Comparable in whole-work burden to Wolf Italian Serenade6 and Dvorak American6, rather than a diploma/professional quartet's broader stamina and technical demands. The substantial fast middle is included in grading; this is not graded as merely a slow nocturne. Full first part and targeted all-part comparisons inspected; medium confidence reflects no complete page-by-page comparison of every lower part.

findings.finding: Independently downloaded and visually inspected all four score pages, bars1–75, Hitoshi Araki engraving. Four cello staves throughout; Adagio, D major. First/second melodic roles use tenor and occasional treble clef; exposed chromatic legato and occasional ornamented subdivisions; lower parts sustain double stops and harmonic support, including changing clefs near the close. First cello carries the longer high cantabile line.

grade.basis: Advanced5 (approximately ABRSM8/RCM9 cello). Secure upper-register cantabile, smooth position changes, chromatic pitch placement, ornaments and sustained soft bow control are needed, especially first cello. The Adagio pace, short length, largely sustained accompaniment and clear shared phrasing keep this below pre-diploma6 anchors overall. Tuning of sustained four-cello chords and balanced melodic handoffs matter, but do not justify an additional full level above the leading player's5 demand. Whole score inspected, including close and brief fast subdivisions; grade is not derived from a professional recording or the prayerful title.

findings.finding: Visually inspected official publisher opening score preview: Cucaraccia and Fugue for four Violas, first movement Cucaraccia, quarter144. Four numbered staves with staggered pizzicato ostinato entrances, rhythmic rests and open-string instructions, then first-viola solo in high treble register with chromatic/grace-note inflections and trill while other parts sustain the rhythmic texture.

Second official preview is printed scorep6, showing contrapuntal four-part writing, staggered entries and rests, chromatic lines, arco transitions, upper first-viola climactic line and final coordinated ritardando/chords. This is a nonconsecutive preview, not the complete score.

grade.basis: Pre-diploma6 first-viola demand inferred from exposed high-register ornamented solo writing and fast, rhythmically precise changes of texture; raise one for independence of four ostinato/contrapuntal voices, exact rests, pizzicato/arco coordination and chromatic ensemble intonation. Diploma7 sits above the more straightforward6 quartet anchors without claiming the sustained technical complexity of Ravel/Debussy8. Two official pages, including first and final music, support medium confidence; intervening Fugue pages unseen, so no invented range maximum or specific intervening technique is asserted.

findings.finding: Independently downloaded and visually inspected publisher's opening score page: Fantasie for Four Violas, York Bowen, editor Thomas Tatton, Grave. Four viola staves; first viola has repeated slurred semiquaver-triplet arpeggios, second/third carry expressive upper-register chromatic lines, fourth has sustained double stops. This establishes exact scoring and some technique, but only opening seven bars are visible.

Label's work-specific note confirms E-minor Op41No1 four-viola Fantasia and a single arch with fast central music and elegiac close. Supports assessing the whole arch rather than only the Grave opening; does not expose notation or enough technical detail to establish its hardest part independently.

grade.basis: Provisional diploma7 expectation from the chromatic upper-register ensemble idiom, continuous arpeggio bow control visible at the opening, and work-specific evidence of a contrasting fast central section; this is a calibrated hypothesis, not an approved grade. The first-page excerpt cannot establish the whole work's highest player demand or whether first viola is harder overall; balanced is provisional because visible demands divide across first–third. No unseen double stops, passagework, register maximum or ensemble uplift are claimed. Hold level and hardestPart until later score sections or dependable direct familiarity can support them; do not import this low-confidence number.

resume.notes: Completed seven blind assessments: six approved, Bowen held with explicitly provisional low-confidence grade. No source research or other reviewer files opened.
